newsitem.title: USA: U.S. brings two drug suspects from Thailand.
newsitem.headline: U.S. brings two drug suspects from Thailand.

text.p: Two alleged Southeast Asian heroin trafficking kingpins were being brought from Thailand to the United States on Friday to stand trial, the State Department announced.
Lieu Wei Ming and Chang Yin Lung, were believed to have been major figures in the drug-running operations of warlord Khun Sa's United Shan Army, department spokesman John Dinger said.

"The United States wants to thank the Royal Thai Government for its superb cooperation in helping bring Liu and Chang to justice," he said in a statement. "This is yet another example of the success of our joint efforts to staunch the flow of illegal heroin from Southeast Asia..."
Both suspects have been indicted on heroin smuggling charges in the United States. They were being brought by U.S. agents to stand trial in a federal court in New York.
Chang was arrested in October 1995 in an operation codenamed "Tiger Trap," carried out in pursuit of a U.S. federal indictment against Khun Sa and 19 of his henchmen.
Liu, arrested in northern Thailand in March, was indicted in an unrelated case involving the shipment of 370 pounds (168 kg) of heroin to New Orleans in August 1993.
